title: mamātmā — My Self
en: You, Maheśa, are ever my own self.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.variants: Focus extract: tvaṃ ca maheśa sadaiva mamātmā. Full verse continues svātmamayaṃ mama tena samastam.

recitation.vowel_lengths: ā in mamātmā from a+a→ā; long e in maheśa; ai in sadaiva from a+e→ai
recitation.articulation: retroflex ṣ in maheśa; ṁ anusvāra in tvaṃ

compounds.tree: mama + ātmā → mamātmā (surface fusion); tvad + anugraha + śakti → tvadanugrahaśakti

members.reading: by the power of Your grace

sandhi.exercise: Reverse mamātmā → mama + ātmā + rule name. Then reverse sadaiva.

syntax.case_roles: tvaṃ (nom); maheśa (voc); mamātmā (nom predicate); tvadanugrahaśaktyā (instr means)
syntax.finite_verbs: bhāti (3sg) in full verse; extract is predicate clause
syntax.implied: copula implied in “You … are … my Self”

translation.literal: You, Maheśa, are always my own Self.
translation.readable: You, Maheśa, are ever my own self — made of You, all is mine through You. (full L2 continues)

trika.abhinavagupta: Bhairavastava is a hymn of grace; the extract isolates Maheśa as one’s own Self.

mapping.trika: address to Śiva as great lord
grace as means of the seeing

trika.bridge: Nominal predication mirrors identity claim — identity is hymn theology, not dictionary ātman.
trika.lakshmanjoo: Not primary for this line; house mealtime lore is Gītā 4.24.
trika.our_synthesis: Pedagogical framing only; L2/L3 from translation-work.

practice.recite: Recite the extract three times; feel a+ā fuse.
practice.write: Write mama and ātmā separately, then fused with the rule.
exercises: Why does ātmā keep long ā?

levels.learn: Hear the line; natural translation; you know “my Self.”
levels.decode: One sandhi proof, vocative, nom predicate, first rule box.
levels.recognise: Grace-power as instrumental in Trika reading.

alternatives: No competing parse of mamātmā; other sites stay open when they arise.
brief: First fusion: mama + ātmā → mamātmā, “my Self.”
logic: Two words, one surface, one reversible rule; identity waits for the proof.
how: Extract for a+ā; full verse for grace as instrumental.
howto: Point at mamātmā; ask what two words hide inside; only then 6.1.101.
sign: Learner reverses the form without the English hint.

rule_boxes.title: Rule box 1 — a + a / a + ā → ā
rule_boxes.body: Adjacent short a (or a + ā) contract to one long ā. Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ. Reverse: split ā into a + a when the words demand it.

rule_boxes.title: Rule box 2 — a + e → ai
rule_boxes.body: yaṇ sandhi: sadā + eva → sadaiva; brahma + eva → brahmaiva. Reverse: ai may hide a + e.

title: namaste viśvamūrtaye — Homage to You
en: Homage to the world-formed, past the world — to ever-shining divinity, to self of unending power.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.variants: Companion drill from v.2: namo namaḥ before n- contexts. L2/L3 as placed.

recitation.articulation: ñ in prapañca; avagraha in svātmane'nantaśaktaye

compounds.tree: namas + te → namaste; viśva + mūrti; sva + ātman + ananta + śakti
compounds.note: v.2 drill: namas → namo before n (namo namaḥ).

sandhi.rule: final s → o before n- (v.2 pattern)

sandhi.exercise: Rewrite namo namaḥ as namas + namas; explain the -o.

syntax.case_roles: datives -āya/-ye “to X”; namas indeclinable; te dative

translation.literal: Homage to the one whose form is beyond the world; to the world-formed, to the ever-divine-shining, to the self of unending power.
translation.readable: Homage to the world-formed, past the world — to ever-shining divinity, to self of unending power.

trika.abhinavagupta: Mahopadeśa opens addressing the one beyond prapañca yet world-formed — homage without a separate devotee object.

mapping.trika: homage whose target is not second
world as form of the one addressed

trika.bridge: Dative can mark addressee while Trika reads addressee as not-other than homage’s subject.
trika.our_synthesis: Pedagogical framing only; L3 from translation-work.

practice.recite: Recite four datives, one per breath.
practice.write: Column namas / namaste / namo namaḥ; mark joints.
exercises: Point out one dat.f and one dat.m.

levels.decode: Dative discovery; namas sandhi; first compound.
levels.recognise: Homage without a second — after the grammar.

alternatives: namas+te standard; stick to layer citation.
brief: Four datives and one indeclinable: “homage to you.”
logic: Learn “to …” on real salutations before charts.
sign: Learner tags every -āya/-ye as dative without being told twice.

title: hṛdi vande — In the heart I bow
en: Bhairava, Lord, refuge of the helpless — with a mind become Yours, in my heart, I bow.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.variants: Extract closes the verse; opening is an acc. object chain.

recitation.vowel_lengths: ṛ vocalic in hṛdi; e in vande

compounds.tree: bhairava + nātha; anātha + śaraṇya; tvad + maya + cittatā

syntax.case_roles: hṛdi loc place; vande acc object chain; tvanmayacittatayā instr means

translation.literal: With mind become Yours, in the heart, I venerate [Bhairava-Lord, refuge of the helpless].
translation.readable: Bhairava, Lord, refuge of the helpless — with a mind become Yours, in my heart, I bow.

trika.abhinavagupta: Interior veneration: instrument is a mind already “become Yours,” not a separate ego.

mapping.trika: mind made of You — non-dual instrument

trika.bridge: Locative says where; Trika reads heart as site where recognition already operates.

exercises: Object of vande and its case?

brief: Locative place + one finite middle verb.
logic: Where? and I do — two-word core first.
how: Full verse when acc. chains are ready.
howto: Discover -i as locative; test on guhāsu later.
sign: Learner tags loc vs instr without a chart.

title: nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati — dances, sings, rejoices
iast: nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍham saṃvit iyam mama …
en: This consciousness of mine dances, sings, rejoices deeply — O Bhairava, Lord.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.variants: Subject saṃvit iyam follows the three verbs in the full verse.

recitation.syllables: ṇṛ-ya-ti | gā-ya-ti | hṛ-ṣya-ti | gā-ḍham | saṃ-vit | i-yam
recitation.vowel_lengths: ā in gāyati, gāḍham; ṛ in nṛtyati
recitation.articulation: retroflex ṇ; ṣ in hṛṣyati; ḍh in gāḍham

sandhi.exercise: Underline every -ti; say what all three share before the key.

syntax.case_roles: three verbs same person/number; saṃvit nom subject; iyam nom f; mama gen

translation.interlinear: dances · sings · rejoices · deeply · consciousness · this · mine
translation.literal: Dances, sings, rejoices deeply — this consciousness of mine.
translation.readable: This consciousness of mine dances, sings, rejoices deeply — O Bhairava, Lord: having won You, my dear…

trika.abhinavagupta: saṃvit is the grammatical subject of dance/song/joy — not the ego alone.

mapping.trika: consciousness as the one who dances

trika.bridge: Three -ti endings first; subject consciousness second; philosophy follows grammar.

practice.write: Three verbs in a column; circle -ti.

levels.recognise: Consciousness as subject — exact by the nominative.

alternatives: iyam as f.nom with saṃvit; layer “indecl.” flag is artifact.
brief: Three verbs, one ending, one philosophical subject.
howto: Hide English; ask “what is dancing?” after -ti.

rule_boxes.title: Rule box 4 — 3sg present often ends -ti
rule_boxes.body: nṛtyati · gāyati · hṛṣyati — same ending, three roots. Discover before the paradigm.

title: mā kiṃcit tyaja — Abandon nothing
source: Abhinavagupta, Anuttarāṣṭikā v.2 (imperative extract); translation-work anuttarastika
iast: mā kiṃcit tyaja mā gṛhāṇa vihara svastho yathāvasthitaḥ
en: Abandon nothing; grasp nothing; live at ease, just as you are.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.variants: Extract from rope-snake verse closing. Full verse: mithyāmohakṛt …

recitation.syllables: mā | kiṃ-ci-tya-ja | mā | gṛ-hā-ṇa | vi-ha-ra | sva-sthaḥ | yathā-va-sthi-taḥ
recitation.vowel_lengths: ā in mā; short u in gṛhāṇa
recitation.articulation: ñ in kiṃcit; ṇ in gṛhāṇa; ṣṭh in yathāvasthitaḥ

sandhi.exercise: Why mā tyaja and not na tyaja?

syntax.case_roles: 2sg imperatives; kiṃcit acc object; svasthaḥ/yathāvasthitaḥ nom describing you

translation.interlinear: do-not · anything · abandon · do-not · grasp · live · healthy · as-standing
translation.literal: Do not abandon anything; do not grasp anything; live at ease, as you stand.
translation.readable: Abandon nothing; grasp nothing; live healthy, staying as you are.

trika.abhinavagupta: After rope-snake diagnosis: if bondage is not real tattvatas, neither grasping nor rejecting is the fix.
trika.bridge: mā+imp is grammar; “live as you are” is the verse’s own practice.

practice.recite: Two mā-prohibitions as a pair, then vihara.
practice.write: na vs mā column; label any invented example “exercise”.

alternatives: L0 morph on long compound noisy — teach imperative core first.
brief: Prohibitions and a command to abide.
sign: Learner chooses mā over na in a new drill.

rule_boxes.title: Rule box 5 — mā + imperative = don’t
rule_boxes.body: Prohibitive mā with imperatives: mā tyaja, mā gṛhāṇa. na negates statements.

title: tvām eva śambhuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye — I take refuge
iast: paraṃ parasthaṃ gahanād anādim | sarvālayaṃ sarvacarācarasthaṃ tvām eva śambhuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye ||
en: Supreme, abiding beyond, depthless, beginningless, one — lodged in many caves, home of all: Śambhu, to You I come for refuge.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.variants: Refuge is second half; epithet chain first. v.3 names Abhinavagupta. passages header range note kept.

recitation.articulation: ṃ in tvām; middle -e on prapadye

members.reading: abiding in all moving and unmoving

compounds.note: Core: acc. chain + 1sg middle refuge verb.

syntax.case_roles: epithet chain facing tvām; śaraṇam acc; prapadye 1sg mid; gahanād abl
syntax.implied: refuge frame “I take refuge in You alone”

translation.interlinear: supreme · beyond-abiding · from-depth · beginningless · one · all-abode · all-moving-unmoving-abiding · you-acc · indeed · Śambhu-acc · refuge-acc · I-resort
translation.literal: Supreme, abiding beyond, from the depth, beginningless, one, entered manifoldly in caves, abode of all, abiding in all moving and unmoving: You alone, Śambhu, refuge — I resort.
translation.readable: Supreme, abiding beyond, depthless, beginningless, one, lodged in many caves, home of all: Śambhu, to You I come for refuge.

trika.abhinavagupta: First act is refuge in Śambhu after absolute epithets; v.3 names author-view.

mapping.trika: qualities of the one in whom refuge is taken

trika.bridge: Acc marks what is taken; non-dual claim comes later in the work, not into the case table.
trika.lakshmanjoo: Lakshmanjoo mealtime is a different text (Gītā 4.24).

practice.recite: Refuge half alone, then two epithets.
practice.write: Mark every acc. in second pāda.
practice.memorise: 1sg middle -e with prapadye as a set.

alternatives: passages header vs v01 locator noted — no silent renumbering.
brief: Accusative objects of refuge; one middle verb.
logic: Cases on a prayer you want to say.
how: Later verses for gen/loc drills (guhāsu loc.pl here).
sign: Learner finds acc and mid in an unseen half-line.

title: tādātmyam anayor … vahnidāhikayor iva — the dual
iast: śaktiś ca śaktimadrūpād vyatirekaṃ na vāñchati | tādātmyam anayor nityaṃ vahnidāhikayor iva ||
en: Power wants no parting from her bearer — never, ever; the two are eternally one — as fire is one with burning.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta

recitation.syllables: śak-tiś ca | śak-ti-mad-rū-pāt | vy-a-ti-re-kaṃ | na vāñ-cha-ti | tā-dāt-myam | a-na-yor | ni-tyaṃ | i-va | va-hni-dā-hi-ka-yor
recitation.articulation: ñ in vāñchati; ṣ in śakti; ḍ in tādātmyam

sandhi.exercise: Circle every -yor; say “dual, of these two.”

syntax.case_roles: śaktiḥ nom; vyatirekam acc; śaktimadrūpāt abl; tādātmyam nom pred; dual gen/loc -yor
syntax.agreement: tādātmyam n.nom.sg; duals limit the pair

translation.interlinear: Power-and-ca · from-power-possessor-form(ABL) · difference(ACC) · not-desires · identity · of-these-two · eternal · as · of-fire-burning-two
translation.literal: Power also does not desire separation from the form of the power-holder. Identity of the two is eternal, as of fire and burning.
translation.readable: Power wants no parting from her bearer — never, ever; the two are eternally one — as fire is one with burning.

trika.abhinavagupta: Śiva–Śakti identity through fire–burning — dual does the work of “exactly two that are not two.”

mapping.trika: fire and burning as irreparable pair

trika.bridge: Dual introduced on Trika’s central analogy; -yor makes metaphysics more exact.

practice.memorise: Dual gen/loc -yor as foundational rule box.

levels.decode: Dual -yor; abl -āt; śaktiś ca; abstract tādātmya.

alternatives: anayor dual; referents from context (śakti & bearer) in syntax.
brief: Dual number through Śiva–Śakti as fire and burning.
logic: New number on a philosophical analogy you already feel.
howto: Predict the ending for “of exactly two”.
sign: Learner tags -yor as dual without a prompt.

rule_boxes.title: Rule box 6 — dual gen/loc = -yor
rule_boxes.body: Exactly two: anayor, vahnidāhikayor. Not plural -ānām / -eṣu.

title: alaṃ bhedānukathayā — Enough of difference-talk (extract)
source: Abhinavagupta, Mahopadeśaviṃśatikā v.8 (first half); translation-work mahopadeshavimshatika
en: Enough of difference-talk — from chewing the sap of devotion to you.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.edition: translation-work mahopadeshavimshatika (gold; L3 song human-review flag)
witness.variants: Extract = first half; full verse in Lesson 9.

recitation.articulation: ṃ in alaṃ; -kth- in anukathā; ṇ in carvaṇāt

members.reading: chewing sap of devotion to you

syntax.case_roles: alaṃ+instr frame; bhedānukathayā instr; tvadbhaktirasacarvaṇāt abl cause

translation.literal: Enough with difference-talk; from chewing the sap of devotion to you.
translation.readable: Enough of difference-talk. From chewing devotion's sap for you —

trika.abhinavagupta: Names bheda as discourse to stop; devotion-rasa is the cause clause.
trika.bridge: Instr and abl do the work; metaphysics waits for Lesson 9.

practice.memorise: alaṃ + instr as reusable frame (exercise substitutes).

logic: Your favourite verse, one mechanism at a time.
sign: Learner infers -ayā as instr ā-stem on a new noun.

rule_boxes.title: Rule box 7 — alaṃ + instrumental = enough of
rule_boxes.body: alaṃ governs the instrumental: alaṃ bhedānukathayā. Substitutes are labelled exercises.

title: Mahopadeśaviṃśatikā 8 — the complete verse
source: Abhinavagupta, Mahopadeśaviṃśatikā v.8 full; translation-work mahopadeshavimshatika
iast: alaṃ bhedānukathayā tvadbhaktirasacarvaṇāt | sarvamekamidaṃ śāntamiti vaktuṃ ca lajjate
en: No more of difference-talk. From chewing devotion's sap for you — all this one, at peace, though saying so is shy.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.edition: translation-work mahopadeshavimshatika L2+L3 (gold; song human-review flag)
witness.variants: Full verse after Lesson 8. C1 essence 7: devotion chewed to sap leaves all as one, at peace.

recitation.syllables: a-laṃ | bhe-dā-nu-ka-tha-yā | tvad-bhak-ti-ra-sa-car-va-ṇāt | sar-va-me-ka-mi-daṃ | śā-nta-mi-ti | vak-tuṃ | ca | laj-ja-te

compounds.note: Full syntax grid; compounds from L8.

sandhi.exercise: Recover all four quarters’ boundaries; mark finite vs non-finite.

syntax.case_roles: alaṃ+instr; abl cause; nom.n chain; inf purpose of lajjate

translation.interlinear: enough · difference-talk(INSTR) · devotion-sap-chewing(ABL) · all-one-this · peace-thus · to-say · even · is-shy
translation.literal: Enough with difference-talk; from chewing the sap of devotion to you, all this is one, at peace — though even to say so is shy.
translation.readable: No more of difference-talk. From chewing devotion's sap for you — all this one, at peace, though even to say so is shy.

trika.abhinavagupta: Difference-discourse stops because bhakti-rasa saturated thought; non-dual claim arrives shyly (C1 essence 7).
trika.bridge: Shyness to say “all is one” is language’s limit — after every case is proven.
trika.our_synthesis: Pedagogical framing; L2/L3/C1 from layers (human-review flag respected).

practice.memorise: No new rule box — reuse L8.

levels.decode: L8 + infinitive + one finite middle + agreement.
levels.recognise: Non-dual claim after proof; C1 as reward.

alternatives: L3 song human-review — faithful placement, no silent retranslation.
brief: Full verse: instr, abl, nom chain, infinitive, one finite verb.
logic: Return to the same Sanskrit with greater understanding.
how: Final exam may contrast with unseen Bodhapañcadaśikā 14.
howto: Deva first; decode; then IAST + analysis.

title: iha jñānaṃ mokṣakāraṇam — Tantrasāra prose
iast: iha jñānaṃ mokṣakāraṇaṃ bandhanimittasya ajñānasya virodhakatvāt
en: Here knowledge is the cause of liberation because it opposes ignorance, the cause of bondage.

witness.deva_source: transliterated from IAST at build (house rule)
witness.author: Abhinavagupta
witness.variants: Syllabus focus sentence; continues dvividhaṃ ca ajñānaṃ… GRETIL NC open — RIGHTS.md.

recitation.syllables: i-ha | jñā-naṃ | mo-kṣa-kā-ra-ṇaṃ | ban-dha-ni-mit-ta-sya | a-jñā-na-sya | vi-ro-dha-ka-tvāt
recitation.articulation: ñ in jñāna; ṣ in mokṣa; dense clusters

compounds.note: Prose stacks genitives; no metrical rescue.

sandhi.exercise: Mark every genitive and the causal ablative.

syntax.case_roles: jñānaṃ nom; mokṣakāraṇam nom pred; gen chain; virodhakatvāt abl of cause
syntax.finite_verbs: none in focus sentence — nominal predication

translation.interlinear: here · knowledge(NOM) · liberation-cause(NOM) · bondage-cause(GEN) · ignorance(GEN) · opposing-ness(ABL)
translation.literal: Here knowledge is the cause of liberation, [because] of being opposed to ignorance, the cause of bondage.
translation.readable: Here knowledge is the cause of liberation because it opposes ignorance, the cause of bondage.

trika.abhinavagupta: Opening causal argument: knowledge opposes ignorance — recognition theme in philosophical prose.
trika.bridge: Ablative of cause builds “because”; Trika content is the jñāna/ajñāna opposition the grammar encodes.
trika.our_synthesis: Pedagogical framing; L2/L3 from tantrasara-a01. GRETIL NC — commercial blocked.

practice.recite: Read aloud twice — flow before compounds.
exercises: What does each genitive attach to?
Build English because-clause in Sanskrit order.

levels.learn: One causal sentence in Sanskrit and English.
levels.decode: Genitives, abstract -tva, causal abl, no finite verb.

alternatives: Machine-proposed gold; focus sentence from syllabus; no invented completion.
logic: From mamātmā to actual philosophical prose.
how: Later Āhnikas; final exam may use Bodhapañcadaśikā 14 unseen.
howto: Parse without IAST; verify; then English.
sign: Learner explains virodhakatvāt from morphology alone.

rule_boxes.title: Rule box 8 — -tva + -āt = because of the fact that
rule_boxes.body: Abstract -tva/-tā then ablative -āt builds causal “because”: virodhakatvāt.
